recipes.name: Best Bourbon Chicken
ingredients_raw: 3 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1 inch pieces
0.25 cup peach-flavored bourbon liqueur (such as Southern Comfort ®)
0.75 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes, or to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a Dutch oven or large, heavy pan. Cook and stir chicken pieces in hot oil until lightly golden on all sides, about 10 minutes. Transfer chicken to a bowl and set aside.

Whisk together water, brown sugar, 3/4 cup fruit juice, soy sauce, ketchup, bourbon liqueur, vinegar, garlic, onion, red pepper flakes, and ginger in the Dutch oven. Bring sauce to a boil while scraping the browned bits of food off the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon.

Stir chicken into sauce, then bring to a full boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until sauce is reduced and thickened and chicken pieces are no longer pink in the middle, about 20 minutes.

Remove chicken pieces to a bowl with a slotted spoon. Stir together 1/4 cup fruit juice with cornstarch in a small bowl until smooth; whisk into sauce, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Bring to a simmer; cook until thickened, about 1 minute. Return chicken pieces to sauce and stir to combine.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Bourbon Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chunks of chicken breast are simmered in a fruity, zesty sauce made with sippin’ whiskey liqueur for a Southern treat.

review.reviewBody: My family is picky to say the least and this was the first thing I have ever made that everyone went back for seconds on. I only made two small changes to cut back on the sweetness. I substituted Jim Beam for the Southern Comfort, and I substituted chicken stock for the fruit juice during the thicken stage at the very end. All in all, this recipe is great!

I altered this a bit otherwise would've given a 5 star. I used less oil in my frying pan that only needed a little for cooking the chicken. For the sauce I made these changes: used less about 1/4 c. less of the brown sugar, used regular apple juice (not the multi fruit blend), used original Southern Comfort, and didn't add the garlic or minced onion to the sauce-- instead I added some fresh chopped onion and the garlic with a little bit of the sauce and cooked a bit then added the rest of the sauce with some carrots and some broccoli then chicken back in with the sauce. Cooked 15-20 minutes and added the cornstarch with some chicken broth instead of the juice like others have done. Served with brown rice and topped with chopped scallions. This was so good will definitely make again.

This was delicious and easy to make. I pretty much followed the recipe, for the fruit juice I took the suggestions of others and used the juice from a canned fruit cocktail I had on hand. I reduced the brown sugar just a bit. Used boneless chicken thighs for moist juicy tender chicken. You don't need to remove the chicken on the final step to thicken the sauce it thickens quick enough. I tossed in some chopped green onions at the end. Served over a bed of fluffy rice. The cooking times were just right for chicken thighs, my chicken was perfectly done. Next time I'll add in some broccoli and red bell pepper. My guys loved it.

Really didn't change anything I did add the juices and chicken stock which cut down the sweetness. Didn't need to use cornstarch because I used season flour and browned the chicken pieces and then everything into the crock pot. All I can say is delish!!

Made exactly as written. Outstanding! second time around, I traded the juice for chicken stock, cut the red pepper flakes to 1/2 tsp., and added a bit more ketchup. That was just to our taste, but the original was great. 

As a side note, I use chicken breasts and found, as other reviewers did, that the meat was a bit dry. The second time, I seared the breasts on each side on a well preheated surface first, then cut into 1" segments before adding back in. That seemed to help a bit.

My boyfriend asked for Bourbon Chicken a year and a half ago for his birthday, and this is what I fixed. I've made it about a dozen times since then, following the recipe more closely sometimes than others. I think I finally got it perfect tonight!
I use a 2.5 lb bag of frozen chicken defrosted in the microwave and then diced, but this generates a lot of water, so I cut the cup of water out entirely.
I've used one packed cup of dark brown sugar before, and that tasted pretty good, but lately I've been sticking with the light brown sugar (which is what the recipe calls for). I only use a loose cup, though, maybe a third of the sugar in a packed cup.
I used straight diet cherry juice and cherry SoCo, too, and that added an amazing rich flavor.
This recipe is definitely a favorite in our house!

I thought this was a little too sweet, even though I already cut down on potential sweetness by replacing the juice with chicken stock. I think using just 3/4 cup of sugar would help next time. I also used chicken thighs instead of chicken breasts and added a little salt and pepper when browning. Served with couscous with a roasted garlic and olive oil seasoning.

Very tasty. We didn't have the fruit concentrate on hand and we don't drink, so we didn't have the Bourbon either. Just left out the Bourbon and blended whole black seedless grapes with some blueberry pancake syrup and chockcherry jam. Still had a nice fruity flavor. Didn't need to use the full 3 pounds of chicken. We just used 3 large chicken breast halves and let simmer uncovered. I imagine that if you do the whole three pounds, you may want to simmer covered if you like your dish more saucy (which we do).

Best eaten when warm as the spicy kick is much more apparent. We have little kids, and when we munched on some of their left overs (I just couldn't let it go to waste), the spicy kick was less pronounced.

Fantastic. I used 2 frozen packs of skinless boneless thighs... About 12-18 of them. When done doing initial cooking of chicken, perhaps I had more broth than I was supposed to, since I ended up with a lot of sauce. had to add more thickener (corn starch mixed in tiny bit of cold water). I also cut up some green peppers and sauteed them separately in some of the sauce then added them to it, was great! Hubby said def. A keeper. Oh, juice- Mott's tot juice fruit punch: look at back- its apple grape &cherry!
Delicious! I also substituted chicken broth for the juice, cut back on the red pepper flakes, as my kids don't like spicy. But I did add green and red peppers and then some green onions at the end.

1.22.2019: Pretty good! Made as written except for tiny bit less red pepper flakes (1/2 tsp. instead of 3/4) and the juice we found was apple-cherry. Fruit juice smelled strong initially, but after reducing and thickening, it was not a noticeable flavor. Chicken did not really brown (3 lb. all at once was more of a boil, even with 11" of surface area), but it we enjoyed the tender outside--and with that sauce it certainly didn't need browning for color. Due to kiddos underfoot, I gathered and whisked all the sauce ingredients in a bowl before starting the chicken; found it did not need any whisking once it was time to add. Served it over caesar salad (like our old place at the mall) and enjoyed that. Had seconds without the salad and that was the only way I noticed a little heat. Next time would do red pepper flakes as written. Yielded about 4 c. of chicken with quite a lot of sauce left over; plenty of sauce to serve with rice if we wanted.
I love this recipe, I added spicy chicken to give a lol more kick.

Excellent flavor! My husband and I tweaked it a bit replacing the juice with a bit of orange juice, grape jelly and maraschino cherry juice ;) We tried "steaming" the chicken separately, which became too dry. Next time we will make chicken along with sauce as directed. Very good!

The family was very satisfied with this recipe. It came together well. I used Jack Daniels Apple in place of peach. I used apple cherry juice because it was all I could find. I’ll make this again. Served with white rice.
I made it as the recipe states. It was too salty for me and I will be reducing the soy sauce the next time I make it.
I was a pretty big fan of this recipe. I added a little extra Southern Comfort and only mixed grape and apple juice but this is an enjoyable recipe to make.

My husband asked for bourbon chicken out of the blue. I’ve never made it before and used this recipe. I’m a vegetarian so I couldn’t taste test this at all while making it. So I followed the recipe hoping I was making it right. When my husband tried it he said it was perfect and exactly what he wanted, my son loved it too. So thanks for the recipe, it was prefect. It was pretty simple to make and that is always a bonus in my book.
Labelled toxic by the EPA on sugar content alone. Its instant diabetes at first bite.
Not even thinking it’s just a sweet and sour sauce for ribs but it has bourbon ! This is not bourbon chicken even close but it’s still ok
I made as written except didn’t have any juice so used chicken broth. Very good but will try with apple juice next time. My picky husband loved it! I also used thighs instead of chicken breast.
